title: 第6章 倾国之力，为君求道
novel_title: 先秦炼气两千年，世人误闯天家
content_zh:
“朕不只要你结成金丹，朕还要你，助朕，也踏上这条长生大道！”

    他终于说出了自己内心最深处的渴望。

    他不要只做一个看着别人长生的凡人。

    他要自己，成为神仙！

    下方的群臣，看着祭台之上，状若癫狂的始皇帝，和神情淡然的顾长青，一个个面面相觑，噤若寒蝉。

    他们听不清皇帝和上卿在说什么。

    但他们能感觉到，有什么东西，要变了。

    这个刚刚统一的帝国，它的未来，似乎要驶向一个无人能够预料的，神秘而未知的方向。

    顾长青看着一脸狂热的嬴政，心中轻轻一叹。

    他知道，嬴政的这个要求，他无法满足。

    修仙，看的是灵根，是资质。

    嬴政早已错过了最佳的修炼年龄，而且他身为帝王，身负亿万子民的因果，龙气缠身，根本无法感应灵气，踏上仙途。

    但是，现在还不是说破的时候。

    他需要嬴政的帮助，来为自己铺平前路。

    “陛下放心。”

    顾长青的语气依旧平静，“臣，定会竭尽所能。”

    他没有答应，但也没有拒绝。

    而这句模棱两可的话，在极度渴望的嬴政听来，却无异于天籁之音。

    泰山封禅之后，始皇帝嬴政返回咸阳。

    一道前所未有的旨意，从咸阳宫发出，如同一阵狂风，席卷了整个刚刚统一的大秦帝国。

    “诏告天下：凡天下方士、炼丹之士、识得奇花异草、知晓上古秘闻者，皆可前来咸阳。一经录用，赏千金，封上造之爵！有大功者，封侯拜将，亦无不可！”

    “令各地郡守，搜罗境内所有古籍、丹方、异闻传说，凡与‘神仙’、‘长生’、‘丹药’相关者，不论真伪，一律誊抄副本，送往咸阳！”

    “令少府，于咸阳城外，建‘求仙宫’，专司此事。一切用度，皆由国库拨付，不受任何官署节制！”

    这几道旨意一出，朝野震动。

    所有人都看出来了，始皇帝陛下，这是真的迷上了长生之道。

    而且，是倾尽整个国家的力量，去追求那虚无缥缥缈的仙缘。

    无数大臣上书劝谏，认为此举劳民伤财，乃是取乱之道。

    其中，以丞相李斯的奏疏最为激烈。

    他认为，帝国初定，百废待兴，应该将国力用在恢复民生，巩固统治上，而不是耗费在这些虚无缥缈的事情上。

    然而，所有的奏疏，都石沉大海，没有得到任何回应。

    嬴政这一次，表现出了前所未有的强硬。

    任何敢于公开反对这件事的人，轻则罢官，重则下狱。

    一时间，朝堂之上，再无人敢对此事多说半个字。

    他们都明白，“长生”，已经成了这位始皇帝心中不可触碰的逆鳞。

    而这场浩大行动的背后，真正的核心，并非那些被征召而来的方士，而是早已回到咸阳，深居简出的上卿，顾长青。……

    咸阳，上卿府。
content_en:
"I not only want you to form a golden elixir, I also want you to help me embark on this road to immortality!"

    He finally expressed his deepest desire.

    He should not just be a mortal who watches others live forever.

    He wants to become a god himself!

    The ministers below looked at the frantic First Emperor and the indifferent Gu Changqing on the altar, and they all looked at each other in silence.

    They couldn't hear clearly what the emperor and the minister were saying.

    But they could feel that something was about to change.

    The future of this newly unified empire seems to be heading in a mysterious and unknown direction that no one can predict.

    Gu Changqing looked at the enthusiastic Ying Zheng and sighed softly in his heart.

    He knew that he could not satisfy Ying Zheng's request.

    Cultivation of immortality depends on spiritual roots and aptitude.

    Ying Zheng has long missed the best age for cultivation, and as an emperor, he is responsible for the karma of hundreds of millions of people. He is surrounded by dragon energy and cannot sense spiritual energy at all and embark on the path to immortality.

    However, now is not the time to tell the truth.

    He needs Ying Zheng's help to pave the way for him.

    "Your Majesty, don't worry."

    Gu Changqing's tone remained calm, "I will do my best, my minister."

    He didn't agree, but he didn't refuse either.

    But to the eager Ying Zheng, these ambiguous words were like the sound of nature.

    After Mount Tai was enshrined in Zen, the First Emperor Ying Zheng returned to Xianyang.

    An unprecedented decree came from Xianyang Palace, like a strong wind, sweeping through the entire newly unified Great Qin Empire.

    "The edict is issued to the world: All the world's scholars, alchemists, those who know strange flowers and herbs, and those who know the secrets of ancient times can come to Xianyang. Once they are hired, they will be rewarded with a thousand gold coins, and they will be given the title of noble! Those who have made great achievements will be granted the title of marquis and general, and there is nothing wrong with it!"

    "Instruct the county guards from all over the country to collect all ancient books, elixir prescriptions, and rumors within the territory. All those related to 'immortals', 'immortality', and 'elixirs', regardless of authenticity, must be copied and sent to Xianyang!"

    "Order the young master to build the 'Qiu Immortal Palace' outside Xianyang City to handle this matter. All expenses will be allocated from the national treasury and will not be controlled by any official agency!"

    As soon as these decrees came out, the government and the public were shocked.

    Everyone could see that His Majesty the First Emperor was really obsessed with the way to immortality.

    Moreover, the entire country has devoted all its strength to pursue that illusory and illusory fairy fate.

    Countless ministers wrote letters to dissuade them, believing that this move wasted money and was a way to cause chaos.

    Among them, Prime Minister Li Si's memorial was the most intense.

    He believed that the empire was in its infancy and was in ruins waiting to be revitalized. The country's power should be used to restore people's livelihood and consolidate rule, rather than expending it on these illusory things.

    However, all memorials fell into disarray and received no response.

    This time, Ying Zheng showed unprecedented toughness.

    Anyone who dares to speak out against this matter will be dismissed from office or jailed at worst.

    For a time, no one in the court dared to say another word about this matter.

    They all understood that "immortality" had become an untouchable evil in the heart of the First Emperor.

    And the real core behind this massive operation was not the conscripted alchemists, but Gu Changqing, the Shangqing who had already returned to Xianyang and lived in seclusion. …

    Xianyang, Shangqing Mansion.
title_en: Chapter 6: Devoting all the strength of the country to seek justice for the king
